why: The Hebrew is the only edition we have in full, and the verses agree closely with 2 Kings 25 and Jeremiah 52. Dropping ten verses on the Greek's evidence alone would be a larger step than the evidence allows, so the Plain English Translation keeps them and flags the choice.
b: The Greek has no 39:4–13: after the officials' names in 39:3 it goes straight to 39:14 (Swete's verse numbers 46:3 to 46:14). No scroll preserves any of these verses. Two explanations are given. Verse 3 and verse 13 both end 'the king of Babylon', so a copyist's eye may have jumped from one to the other (the Greek would then show the effect of a slip in its Hebrew source). Or the Greek's source was the earlier edition and the Masoretic edition filled in the story from Jeremiah 52 and 2 Kings 25. Tov's view that the Greek often shows the earlier edition favors the second; the first has its supporters. Each of the ten verses has its own entry below; they go together.

readings.plain: from Ramah

readings.w: Greek, as printed by Swete (Codex Vaticanus)
readings.plain: from Daman

why: The Hebrew place name Ramah fits the scene, since the exiles were gathered there. Daman is a name known nowhere else in this story, and why the Greek has it is not known; a misreading of the Hebrew name is possible but only a guess.

a: son of Elishama, one of the royal line and one of the king's chief men
t: Elishama and the king's chief men
p: Swete's Greek has 'son of Elasa' and lacks 'the king's chief men'.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008)
readings.orig: בֶּן אֱלִישָׁמָע מִזֶּרַע הַמְּלוּכָה וְרַבֵּי הַמֶּלֶךְ
readings.en: son of Elishama, of the royal seed, and chiefs of the king
readings.plain: son of Elishama, one of the royal line and one of the king's chief men

readings.w: Greek, as printed by Swete (Codex Vaticanus)
readings.orig: υἱοῦ Ἐλασὰ ἀπὸ γένους τοῦ βασιλέως
readings.en: son of Elasa, of the king's family
readings.plain: son of Elasa, of the king's family

why: 2 Kings 25:25 has Elishama and lacks the king's chief men too, so the Greek agrees with 2 Kings on the second point and reads a different name on the first. The Plain English Translation follows the Hebrew of Jeremiah and gives the other readings.

a: You have nothing to fear from serving the Chaldeans
t: Serving the Chaldeans, or the Chaldeans' servants
p: The Hebrew of Jeremiah says 'from serving'; Swete's Greek and 2 Kings 25:24 say 'the Chaldeans' servants'.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008)
readings.en: do not fear from serving the Chaldeans
readings.plain: You have nothing to fear from serving the Chaldeans

readings.w: Greek, as printed by Swete (Codex Vaticanus); 2 Kings 25:24 has Hebrew meavdei, 'servants of'
readings.orig: μὴ φοβηθῆτε ἀπὸ προσώπου παίδων τῶν Χαλδαίων
readings.en: do not fear before the servants of the Chaldeans
readings.plain: Don't fear the Chaldeans' servants

why: The two Hebrew readings differ by one letter (meavod, meavdei). Two witnesses, the Greek and 2 Kings, read 'servants'; the Masoretic Text of Jeremiah reads 'from serving', which fits the next clause, 'serve the king of Babylon'. The Plain English Translation keeps the Hebrew of Jeremiah and names the other reading. The site's 2 Kings 25:24 reads "Don't fear the Chaldeans' servants".

a: Whatever he tells you
t: A written word that is not read
p: The Leningrad text writes an extra word, 'im ('except'), that is not read aloud.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008), Qere (read aloud)
readings.orig: כַּאֲשֶׁר יְדַבֵּר אֵלֶיךָ כֵּן עֲשֵׂה עִמּוֹ
readings.en: just as he says to you, so do with him
readings.plain: Whatever he tells you

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008), Ketiv (written, not read)
readings.en: except as he says to you
readings.plain: Only what he tells you

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Qere. The written 'im would make the order 'do only what he says', which is close in sense. The Greek lacks 39:4-13.

a: he will spread his grand tent over them
p: The written form is shafruro, the read form shafriro.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008), Qere (read aloud)
readings.plain: he will spread his grand tent over them

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008), Ketiv (written)
readings.plain: he will spread his grand tent over them

why: One rare word spelled with two vowels; the sense is the same. The Greek's 'weapons' is a different reading (see the note). 2QJer's word here is restored, not read.

a: He will come and strike the land of Egypt.
t: 'He will come', or 'he will come to it'
p: The written form has an extra ending, 'to it'.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008), Qere (read aloud)
readings.plain: He will come and strike the land of Egypt.

readings.w: Masoretic Text (Leningrad Codex, AD 1008), Ketiv (written); 2QJer (2Q13) writes the same form
readings.en: and he will come to it
readings.plain: He will come to it and strike the land of Egypt.

why: The extra ending adds 'it' (the land) and changes the sense very little. The Plain English Translation follows the Qere.
b: The transcription marks 2QJer's word as differing from the Masoretic consonants only in a vowel letter.
